clue.text: Its selections are bound to finish up in literary posts

definitions.text: Its selections are bound to finish up in literary posts

parts.words: Its selections are bound to finish up in literary posts
parts.note: a society whose chosen titles are bound volumes, delivered to members through the post

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'certain to', but it means hardbound; 'posts' is the mail, through which a subscription society sends its chosen books.
explanation.definitionFit: A subscription society picks hardback titles and mails them to its members, so its picks are bound volumes arriving by post.

clue.text: Swearword disturbed old boy

indicators.note: disturbed suggests the letters of old boy are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: An old school chum is upset and lets fly with a curse.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective is a classic mild British expletive, used as an intensifier in cursing.

clue.text: With nothing originally, a Scottish inventor raised capital

indicators.note: originally places the zero at the very start of the answer

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: raised, in a down clue, means the following letters read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: James Watt, the Scottish engineer who improved the steam engine

explanation.surface: A Scottish inventor with nothing to his name nevertheless raises funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns A + WATT upwards to give TTAWA, and O for nothing comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the seat of government of Canada, its national capital city.

clue.text: Leader of crazy expedition, pure and simple

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: expedition can mean speed or promptness, i.e. haste

explanation.surface: Someone heads a mad venture and calls it pure and simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expedition' looks like a journey, but here it is the older sense of speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means sexually pure, and of artistic style it means plain and unadorned.

clue.text: Work little as pupil? Be prepared to take part if necessary

definitions.meaning: first meaning, whimsically: to study too little

definitions.text: Be prepared to take part if necessary
definitions.meaning: second meaning: to learn a role so as to stand in for an actor

explanation.walkthrough: The first half splits the word as UNDER STUDY, a pupil doing too little; the second is the theatrical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre, a stand-in learns another actor's role so they can perform it whenever the principal is unavailable.

clue.text: City hospital is minister's responsibility

parts.note: Paris, capital city of France
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A clergyman is put in charge of a city hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister of a church has pastoral care of a local district and its congregation.

clue.text: Contribution to original thoughts, however

indicators.note: Contribution to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone contributes to a set of original ideas, with reservations.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are conjunctions or adverbs that introduce a concession, a contrasting statement.

clue.text: Freedom from punishment –- I am powerless without it

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm

indicators.note: without in its older sense of outside, so the weak word goes around it

parts.note: powerless means weak, puny

explanation.surface: Someone confesses being helpless without a certain thing that grants immunity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking, so it is a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Impunity is exemption from penalty or harmful consequences for one's actions.

clue.text: Persistently bothering prince in middle of night

parts.note: Prince Harry of the British royal family

indicators.note: the middle of a five-letter word is its third letter

explanation.surface: A royal keeps pestering someone in the dead of night.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to harass or pester repeatedly, so this participle means continually troubling.

clue.text: Manoeuvre to draw us away from the centre

indicators.note: to manoeuvre is to shift things around, so the letters of to draw us are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A tactic intended to lure us away from the middle ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes motion directed toward the outside, from the middle toward the edges.

clue.text: Lethargy produced by Proust novel

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the author's name is made new by rearranging it

explanation.surface: Reading a long Proust novel induces drowsiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book by Proust, which makes the surface plausible, but it is the rearrangement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed, torpid state of near unconsciousness, akin to extreme sluggishness.

clue.text: Economic decline making part of Ireland act

parts.note: County Down is in Northern Ireland
a turn is a performer's act on stage

explanation.surface: A recession is caused by one region of Ireland taking action.
explanation.walkthrough: Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland; a turn is a variety act.
explanation.definitionFit: A downturn is a fall in business activity or prices, a recessionary slump.

clue.text: Prize captured by Christian

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a reward, as offered for a capture
second meaning: HMS ..., the ship seized by mutineers led by Fletcher Christian

explanation.walkthrough: 'Christian' looks like a believer, but it is Fletcher Christian, who led the 1789 mutiny on the ship of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: A bounty is a reward paid out, and it is also the famous ship taken over by its mutinous crew.

clue.text: Like joint with piano, nice

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
articular is the anatomical adjective meaning relating to joints

explanation.surface: Something resembling a joint, set beside a piano, looks pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nice' here is its older sense of fussy or finely discriminating, not pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice in its old sense means fastidious or exacting, just as a fussy person is choosy.

clue.text: Stop going round the bend –- it can be shattering

indicators.note: it can be says the following word may become something else, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Losing one's mind is exhausting, and stopping it could be too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattering' looks like 'exhausting', but it is the word whose letters are rearranged; 'it can be' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove the curve from a road or rod is to make it run in a line, so it no longer bends.

clue.text: Quick service provided before second helping?

parts.note: what comes before second is first
helping as a noun meaning help, assistance, i.e. aid

explanation.surface: A speedy waiter brings the first course before second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helping' looks like a portion of food, but it means assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergency treatment is the prompt care given to an injured person before a doctor arrives.

clue.text: Number ten's position in deadlock

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in rugby union the fly-half, who wears shirt number 10
second meaning: an impasse where neither side gives way

explanation.walkthrough: 'Number ten' suggests Downing Street, the Prime Minister's residence, but it is a rugby shirt number.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-off is a stalemate, and also the rugby half-back between scrum-half and the centres.

clue.text: Directions I needed to get into a computer lacking memory

indicators.note: to get into means these letters are placed inside the others

parts.note: a Mac is an Apple computer
N, E and S are compass directions, north, east and south

explanation.surface: Instructions are needed to get into a computer short of memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Directions' looks like instructions, but it gives compass points N, E, S, which go with I inside A MAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone suffering from amnesia has lost their recall, so they are without remembrance.

clue.text: I'd got in very close to be threatening

indicators.note: got in says the contraction is put inside the other word

parts.note: intimate means very close, as of friends
I'd without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone admits getting very close in order to menace.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimidate is to frighten or menace someone into doing what one wants.

clue.text: Put one over on old fool outside university

indicators.note: the old fool sits outside, so the university letter goes within it

parts.note: a twit is a fool

explanation.surface: Someone tricks a silly old man standing outside a college.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwit is to get the better of someone by cleverness, i.e. to trick them.

clue.text: Some worship a god ardently in temple

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Certain people fervently worship a deity in a shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'in temple' as the definition; 'in' is only a link word, so the definition is 'temple'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower built as a Buddhist or Hindu sacred building in Asia.

clue.text: Brave grabbing European in nasty way

indicators.note: grabbing means the brave word holds the European letter inside it

parts.note: manly means brave, courageous

explanation.surface: A brave fighter seizes a European in a spiteful fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means unkindly or spitefully, behaving with a petty, ungenerous spirit.

clue.text: Paper ready to go when evening starts

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
set means ready, as in 'all set'

explanation.surface: The newspaper is printed and ready for delivery as night falls.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British daily tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk, the time the sun goes down, marks the onset of the night-time hours.

clue.text: Copper involved in a case? Right

indicators.note: involved in means the metal's symbol is wrapped inside the other letters

parts.note: a crate is a packing case
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Is a policeman caught up in a criminal case? Correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman involved in a legal case, but it is the element; 'case' is a crate.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means correct or precise, as in a correct answer.

clue.text: Handsome youth, extremely awkward, often impetuous

indicators.note: extremely means take the extremes, first and last letters, of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A good-looking young man, very gauche and frequently rash.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Adonis was the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite, so his name means a beautiful young man.

clue.text: Information on start of strike, or less extreme action

indicators.note: on means the information comes after, sitting on the first letter
the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: lowdown is informal for the relevant facts, information

explanation.surface: News of a strike starting, or of a milder protest.
explanation.walkthrough: A go-slow, in which workers deliberately work slowly, is industrial action milder than a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers' deliberate go-slow is a protest stopping short of a full walkout.

clue.text: Failing to cross to other side

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a flaw or shortcoming (noun)
second meaning: to desert one's country or party for the opposing one (verb)

explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning flaw.
explanation.definitionFit: A defect is a fault, and to defect is to abandon one's allegiance and join the opposition.

clue.text: Dry area surrounded by sea in part of Europe

indicators.note: surrounded by means the dry letters and area letter sit within the sea word

parts.note: the briny is a colloquial name for the sea
TT, teetotal, means abstaining from alcohol, i.e. dry

explanation.surface: A dry district encircled by water somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: TT stands for teetotal, so dry; the briny is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Brittany is a peninsular region of north-west France, so it lies within that continent.
